- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via timeoutMs (symbol, a field of interface ProbeClusterDriverHealthOptions))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via automation.trigger (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /automation/trigger/:name, selected by route anchor /trigger/:name), /trigger/:name (route, bridged from symbol timeoutMs — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **31** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ee492c12222adc6570a81eaf5fff7c0ef75c071e` — the merge of head `eddeda2669372f860f711f81681ac43cc5e62bbc` into base `b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ee492c12222adc6570a81eaf5fff7c0ef75c071e && git checkout ee492c12222adc6570a81eaf5fff7c0ef75c071e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923 eddeda2669372f860f711f81681ac43cc5e62bbc && git checkout -B drift-repro b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923 && git merge --no-ff eddeda2669372f860f711f81681ac43cc5e62bbc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b126c13065db29c80996efc7e0527a40f651c923` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `eddeda2669372f860f711f81681ac43cc5e62bbc`
Local-runs: none

The face is the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` declaration alone. No published schema and no governed path are in the tree, and no narrowing is declared. Inputs: card #31601 (body, comments, claim 6727414288, amendment 6728245404, os-dev-report 6728231834), the PR's file list and net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`GET /ready` 200 body, declared multi-node on the redis driver:** the body gains `cluster: { driver, reachable, reason? }`. With the store reachable `status` stays `'ready'`; unreachable gives `status: 'degraded'` and still 200 (PM decision D4). This is a widening of the response on that topology only. Right.
- **Gate:** `clusterReadiness` reads only when `declaresMultiNode(process.env)` (the predicate the split-brain guard and the shared cache already read) AND `probeClusterDriverHealth(cluster, 'redis')` finds a redis connection. Otherwise it answers `undefined`, and `withClusterReading` returns the same body object. Both halves of #3814 R3 hold. Right.
- **Single node, memory driver, no cluster service:** byte-identical body and status; the store is never probed. Right, pinned.
- **503 paths:** the booting/stopping 503 and the primary-datasource 503 return before `clusterReadiness` is consulted. Unchanged. Right.
- **#13408 secondary-datasource branch:** keeps its `degraded: { drivers, primaryDatasource }` object and gains the `cluster` entry. `status` turns `'degraded'` only when the store is unreachable. Right (seat ruling in 6728245404).
- **Disclosure:** `reason` is a closed set (`timeout`, `ping-failed`, `unexpected-reply`, `no-probe`). The client's error text, which names host and port, never reaches the anonymous body. Right.
- **Cost:** one `PING` raced against a 500 ms unref'd timer; a late rejection is observed, not unhandled. Memoized 1 s, including the "not applicable" answer. Right.
- **New public names in `@objectstack/service-cluster`:** `probeClusterDriverHealth`, `DEFAULT_CLUSTER_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` and three types. Additive. Names are the seat's call and are kept (6728245404). Right.

### ② Semver level

The changeset puts `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/service-cluster` at patch, with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The change is an additive response field on one topology plus an additive export. Patch matches the repo's practice for additive server surface. `@objectstack/runtime` already depends on `@objectstack/service-cluster` (`workspace:*`), so no manifest change is needed. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Open question 1 (export names and the `cluster` key): kept.
- Open question 2 (`'ready'` for the healthy declared case): kept.
- Open question 3 (the #13408 branch status): kept as built.
- Docs: the amendment added `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx` and `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`. Read sentence by sentence against the code, both agree:
  - the two 200 shapes;
  - 200 not 503, with D4's reason;
  - the closed `reason` set;
  - no address in the body;
  - 500 ms `PING` cached about 1 s;
  - consulted only on the 200 paths;
  - single node / memory / no cluster unchanged and never probed;
  - `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER` alone is not a declaration, which matches `declaresMultiNode`.
- Dev deviations: `driver-turso` built for the runtime typecheck; a mistaken `OS_SKIP_DTS` build was stopped and rebuilt with DTS before the final gates; ablation A4 was re-run after a tool refusal; dogfood ran on `04ca432f`, and the later commits only touch a test file and docs. None changes the judgment. CI on this head is the gate verdict.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-niooue`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmP8JJo4zF2sjTBRwnX`

**VERDICT: PASS**
